STEMI_late_presentation.recommendation: In patients with a working diagnosis of STEMI and a time from symptom onset >12 h, a PPCI strategy is recommended in the presence of ongoing symptoms suggestive of ischaemia, haemodynamic instability, or life‑threatening arrhythmias.
STEMI_late_presentation.notes: Applies when ongoing ischemic symptoms, instability, or arrhythmias are present despite symptom onset >12 h.

Routine_PCI_of_occluded_IRA.recommendation: Routine PCI of an occluded IRA is not recommended in STEMI patients presenting >48 h after symptom onset and without persistent symptoms.
Routine_PCI_of_occluded_IRA.notes: Specifically refers to routine intervention for occluded infarct‑related artery (IRA) beyond 48 h when no persistent symptoms.

Transfer_interventions_after_fibrinolysi.recommendation: Transfer to a PCI‑capable centre is recommended in all patients immediately after fibrinolysis.
Transfer_interventions_after_fibrinolysi.notes: Routine immediate transfer post‑fibrinolysis for further care and potential intervention.

Transfer_interventions_after_fibrinolysi.recommendation: Emergency angiography and PCI of the IRA, if indicated, is recommended in patients with new‑onset or persistent heart failure/shock after fibrinolysis.
Transfer_interventions_after_fibrinolysi.notes: Indication based on clinical instability (heart failure/shock) after fibrinolysis.

Transfer_interventions_after_fibrinolysi.recommendation: Angiography and PCI of the IRA, if indicated, is recommended between 2 and 24 h after successful fibrinolysis.
Transfer_interventions_after_fibrinolysi.notes: Timing guidance for angiography after successful fibrinolysis.

Invasive_strategy_in_NSTE-ACS.recommendation: An invasive strategy during hospital admission is recommended in NSTE‑ACS patients with high‑risk criteria or with a high index of suspicion for unstable angina.
Invasive_strategy_in_NSTE-ACS.notes: Applies to patients identified as high‑risk or highly suspicious for unstable angina.

Invasive_strategy_in_NSTE-ACS.recommendation: A selective invasive approach is recommended in patients without very high‑ or high‑risk features and a low index of suspicion for NSTE‑ACS.
Invasive_strategy_in_NSTE-ACS.notes: Suggests conservative/selective strategy for lower‑risk presentations.

Invasive_strategy_in_NSTE-ACS.recommendation: An immediate invasive strategy is recommended in patients with a working diagnosis of NSTE‑ACS and with at least one of the following very high‑risk criteria: haemodynamic instability or cardiogenic shock; recurrent or refractory chest pain despite medical treatment; in‑hospital life‑threatening arrhythmias; mechanical complications of MI; acute heart failure presumed secondary to ongoing myocardial ischaemia.
Invasive_strategy_in_NSTE-ACS.notes: Lists very high‑risk criteria that mandate immediate invasive strategy; also notes recurrent dynamic ST‑segment or T wave changes, particularly intermittent ST‑segment elevation.
